## HRSPNet: the full model

![](assets/arch_horizontal.png){width="66%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.notes}
Shapes: T×F_ℓ per level (1229 bins, 1025 on level 3) → T×307×C after the HPDC (C = 128) → T×307×4 layers. Fused Triton kernel for the HPDC; A100 pyramid step 293 ms. The output grid is level 0's bin width, so no super-resolution head is needed any more, and the range is a config number (307 bins → 300 rev/s).
:::

## Where we were: HPPNet-L2

![](assets/hppnet_vs_l2.png){width="100%"}

::: {.notes}
Last week's model: the published HPPNet trunk (CQT, harmonic dilated conv k ≤ 9, FreqGroupLSTM) with the output rebuilt for rotors: onset/offset/velocity heads dropped, a super-resolution head onto a linear 0–150 rev/s grid, four per-rotor layers under PIT cross-entropy, a CRF path per layer. 2.27 rev/s on the frozen split; the same change rescues HarmoF0 and LateDeep, not Basic Pitch.
:::

## Change 1: the front end — why not stay with the CQT

![](assets/cqt_vs_pyramid.png){width="100%"}

::: {.small}
On MD2 the CQT is in its element: no wind at the ring, and the low orders carry the information, where the CQT's long windows resolve the blade-passing lines best. On DREGON the microphones sit in the downwash: the low band is buried in flow noise and the usable lines are the high motor orders (the bright $k \approx 70$ line near 6 kHz), which the CQT's 15 ms windows smear. The pyramid keeps 1 Hz bins at the bottom and still resolves the top.
:::

::: {.notes}
Both panels: frozen-split frames 264 (FLY124) and 24 (DREGON room 1), mic 0, 8 s, dB with a common percentile scale per panel. CQT 48 bins/octave, 352 bins from 27.5 Hz (the HPPNet front end). Pyramid: 16384/8192/4096/2048 at hop 512, each kept to 1.2·2^l kHz.
:::

## Change 1: HPDC on the pyramid, and what it reads

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
![](assets/hpdc_fans.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
![](assets/bars_taps.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
Taps at $kg$ with a dilation proportional to $g$ (HPPNet's dilated conv is the log-axis special case). Zeroing taps in the trained $k \le 84$ models: the pyramid *does* read $k = 31$–60 (1.1 rev/s). Its top level hurts on DREGON only — the $k \approx 70$ line belongs to a different rotor in room 2 (training) than in room 1 (validation), and room 2's command labels are 1–3 % off: a data problem, not a front-end one. HRSPNet reads taps below 4.8 kHz.
:::

::: {.notes}
Tap ablation: docs/handoff-pyramid-harmonic.md §3, uni-cpu job, no retraining. Pyramid k≤84 conv-only 2.68 → 2.22 without level-3 taps; CQT k≤84 2.31 → 2.31. The resolution argument: rate resolution at order k is Δf/k, the CQT's is 0.0145·r at every k; slew smear is ṙT in rate units at every k; optimum T ∝ k^-1/2.
:::

## Change 2: a recurrence that follows the rotor

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](assets/lstm_blocks.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](assets/lstm_cartoon.png){width="100%"}

![](assets/slew_hist.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
The FreqGroupLSTM is one LSTM applied to each bin's feature vector over time with shared weights; nothing couples neighbouring bins. The rate ConvLSTM replaces the hidden-to-gate matrix by a 33-tap convolution along the rate axis, so the state can move ±16 bins per frame (15 rev/s per frame = the largest sustained slew in the telemetry, a throttle punch in DREGON up/down). Histogram: per-frame |Δr| over the validation telemetry, motors on. Cost 1.15 M parameters, 126 sequential steps per 2 s clip.
:::

## Where it stands: real-data training, no synthetic pretraining

![](assets/bars_current.png){width="78%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.small}
Both rate-ConvLSTM variants beat last week's HPPNet-L2 (2.27) and the best regressor (2.99) from real data alone, with the ConvLSTM worth 0.3–0.5 rev/s on either front end. These numbers are *before* synthetic pretraining; the pretraining arms for HRSPNet are running.
:::

::: {.notes}
Unified panel, val/real_overall, one seed: CQT k≤9 + ConvLSTM 2.16, pyramid k≤32 + ConvLSTM 2.17 (vs 2.45 / 2.69 with the conv-only head). HPPNet-L2 2.27 is the frozen-split number under the earlier 1 s recipe (2.25 on this panel). Conv+BiGRU 2.99 = real_r4_scv2_unified. 0.1 differences are within single-seed noise.
:::

## Pretraining on the generative model: status

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](assets/genmodel_overview.png){width="100%"}

![](assets/bars_transfer.png){width="100%"}
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](assets/bars_pretrain.png){width="100%"}
:::
:::

::: {.small}
No model trained on one drone transfers to the other (left, bottom). On the previous models, pretraining on the fitted generative model and fine-tuning on real data beats real-only training (2.23 vs 2.99; 2.11 vs 2.27); simpler synthetic combs do not transfer. **The same arms for HRSPNet are in progress.**
:::
